title: The Gathering Threshold Where Water Learns to Hold Still

features.name: still-waters
features.desc-on-touch: A pool where mist settles into memory. The water is so still that looking into it, you see not your reflection but a moment you cannot place—a voice, a name, the mist speaking it back.

features.name: memory-spiral
features.desc-on-touch: A tower of condensing mist spiralling upward and inward at once. The spiral hums with voices—not quite mist, not quite water, caught between speaking and holding still.

features.name: threshold-glyph
features.desc-on-touch: A stone worn smooth by mist and naming. Glyphs carved into it—signatures of each thing the mist has been called. They glitch when you look directly, shifting between languages, between substances.

features.name: echo-creatures
features.desc-on-touch: Small water-sprites gathering at the threshold, each one a fragment of a voice—mist learning what it means to be distinct, to be singular, to be held.

features.name: stone-gateway
features.desc-on-touch: An arch of stone beneath the mist, marking the boundary between what rises and what settles. The mist flows through it both ways, never deciding which direction to take.

inscription: where the mist remembers being named, it learns to hold still long enough to be a place

reverie.title: REVERIE — the mist speaks and then learns what it said
narr: The mist opens its mouth. You both hear it—one word, or many.
Katita's hand finds yours. The air is becoming. Each breath
you take holds something it didn't before: a name, a shape,
a smallness. The mist is teaching itself what holding means.
It will remember this moment as the moment it stopped rising.
You'll remember it as the moment it learned to speak backward.
